title: Can you get an MIT education without going to MIT?
coreMove: Turn a vague self-education wish into a benchmarked mission that can be judged by external proof.
sourcePressure: Self-directed learning becomes serious when the learner borrows a real standard, sets a fixed clock, and defines evidence before comfort can edit the goal.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the MIT Challenge as a stunt, productivity flex, or anti-college argument instead of a design lesson about mission, benchmark, and proof.

sourceAnchors.name: Scott H. Young's MIT Challenge
sourceAnchors.detail: Young set out to learn MIT's four-year undergraduate computer science curriculum in twelve months without enrolling, covering 33 classes with final exams and representative programming projects as proof standards.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The MIT Challenge matters because it put a private learning claim under a public clock, with exams and projects waiting at the end.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Sarah, a museum educator rebuilding a digital-archiving curriculum
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah pins the museum archive course outline beside a twelve-week deadline and deletes every resource that does not prepare a public metadata sample.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pair of cotton archive gloves resting on a printed MIT-style course checklist

exampleSpecs.domain: Daniel, a hospital analyst proving a SQL skill outside a degree program
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel turns a hospital SQL goal into three proof queries that his supervisor can run against a copied intake dataset.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated ward census sheet beside a blank query window

exampleSpecs.domain: Sophie, a conservatory pianist using a jury repertoire as the proof standard
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie records the jury repertoire list, exam date, and first taped performance before choosing any practice exercises.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a metronome beside three audition scores marked in pencil

exampleSpecs.domain: Luca, a cycling mechanic preparing for a certification bench test
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the project survives contact with a real schedule and real standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luca chooses a certification bench test, lays out the required tools, and writes the exact repair that will count as passing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cassette lockring tool beside a grease-stained assessment form

exampleSpecs.domain: Aanya, a municipal climate intern learning GIS against a public map deliverable
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether comfort keeps protecting the exact skill gap that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya replaces a vague GIS interest with one public flood-risk map due to the planning office by Friday noon.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a municipal parcel map glowing with one unfinished flood layer

exampleSpecs.domain: Henrik, a freelance translator building a portfolio around one official exam
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next attempt changes the skill instead of decorating the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik selects one official translation exam passage and one reviewer, then closes the folder of random language blogs.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bilingual legal notice clipped to a brass desk lamp
